title: Runtime: add model-family detection rules from model metadata (with safe unknown fallback)
author: Grace Kim
body: Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 needs a stable, explicit notion of “model family” that we can use as a key in the registry table (family x seq-bucket x GPU). Today we infer architecture ad-hoc in a few callsites and it’s not deterministic across metadata sources (HF config vs internal catalog), which makes perf debugging painful and increases the chance of picking an unsafe kernel for unknown models. This PR introduces a single model-family detection module that maps model metadata -> ModelFamilyId + a small set of normalized flags relevant to selection. What’s included: (1) A deterministic mapping function `DetectModelFamily(metadata)` that uses (in order) explicit `redwood.model_family` override, HF `model_type`, HF `architectures`, and a small set of heuristics for commonly-onboarded families; (2) Normalization of attention-related flags used downstream: grouped-query attention (via `num_key_value_heads < num_attention_heads`), sliding-window attention, and RoPE scaling mode (linear/dynamic) where present; (3) A safe fallback behavior for unknown/partial metadata: returns `ModelFamilyId::Unknown` and `SafetyClass::SafeOnly`, which forces the selector to pick from the safe kernel set (or fall back to selector v1 depending on config); (4) Unit tests with representative configs for Llama-family, Mistral-family, Qwen-family, plus “unknown family” and “conflicting metadata” cases; (5) Minimal wiring into the selector v2 context so that the chosen family + flags are carried through and can be emitted in selector telemetry (telemetry emission itself lands in a follow-up PR). Notes on determinism: the mapping is pure and stable for identical metadata; tie-breaking is explicit (override > model_type > architectures > heuristic). The intent is not to perfectly classify every open model on day 1, but to make unknown behavior safe and observable while we add families incrementally. Rollout/compat: no customer-facing changes; this codepath is only used by selector v2 (feature-flagged) and returns Unknown when metadata is missing rather than throwing. Follow-ups: add additional families (Phi/Gemma/DeepSeek) as we onboard them; plumb the SafetyClass into the v2 registry lookup logic to restrict kernel candidates for Unknown/experimental cases.
commits: runtime/model-family: introduce ModelFamilyId enum + ModelMetadata struct
runtime/model-family: implement DetectModelFamily() mapping rules + tie-break precedence
runtime/selector-v2: plumb model family + flags into SelectionContext
tests: add fixture HF configs and unit tests for known/unknown families
docs(internal): add comment block describing mapping inputs and precedence
implementation_details: Mapping precedence: `metadata.redwood.model_family` (if present) -> `hf.model_type` -> `hf.architectures[0]` -> heuristic hints (e.g., tokenizer_name/model_name patterns only when explicitly provided by internal catalog).
Known families added in this PR: Llama-family (llama, llama2/3 variants), Mistral-family (mistral, mixtral), Qwen-family (qwen2).
GQA detection: `num_key_value_heads` present and `num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads` => set `attn.gqa=true` and compute `kv_head_ratio` for debug only (not used as a selection key yet).
Sliding window: parse `sliding_window` (when present) and treat as a selection-relevant flag because it changes attention behavior for long contexts.
RoPE scaling: parse `rope_scaling.type` + factor; normalize to enum; do not reject unknown values—store as `RopeScaling::Unknown` and rely on SafeOnly fallback when combined with Unknown family.

Unknown behavior: return `ModelFamilyId::Unknown` and `SafetyClass::SafeOnly` (downstream can choose safe kernel list or fall back to selector v1 depending on config). No exceptions thrown for missing fields.
Conflicting metadata behavior: if `model_type` and `architectures` map to different families, prefer `model_type` and emit a debug-only note via `SelectionDebugInfo` (not logged by default).
testing: Unit: model_family_detection_test covers: llama3, mistral, qwen2, unknown-minimal, conflicting metadata, explicit redwood override.
Build: runtime-linux-x86_64 and runtime-cuda-sm80/90 compile targets.
Manual: ran selector-v2 dry-run locally against 12 internal catalog entries; verified stable family ids and that missing metadata yields Unknown + SafeOnly.
review_conversation: Noah Patel: Can we guarantee determinism and avoid model-name string heuristics? I’m worried about subtle changes in catalog names changing behavior. Grace Kim: Agree—string heuristics are only used when internal catalog explicitly provides `model_name_hint` (optional) and are not applied to raw HF configs. Precedence is override > model_type > architectures > (optional) hint. Added a test to ensure we don’t consult hint unless it’s explicitly present.

Yuki Sato: For unknown family, do we want to return Unknown but still expose parsed flags? Might help later. Grace Kim: Yes, we still parse flags best-effort; Unknown + SafeOnly is the gate. Added `RopeScaling::Unknown` handling and ensured missing fields don’t crash.

Omar El-Sayed: Please wire through an explicit “safety class” so scheduler/runtime can reason about safe kernels vs v1 fallback. Grace Kim: Added `SafetyClass` to `SelectionContext` and plumbed it; actual enforcement is in ENG-3923 (selector core) but context is ready.

Anika Gupta: Add a test for NaN-risky combinations? At least cover that unknown metadata never selects non-safe kernels. Grace Kim: Added unit coverage for Unknown -> SafetyClass::SafeOnly. Kernel conformance coverage lands in ENG-3928; linking it in the PR description.
release_notes: Internal only: adds deterministic model-family detection for selector v2; unknown/partial metadata maps to Unknown + SafeOnly for safe fallback behavior.
